questions.instruction: Compare these two Amazon-themed emails. Which one is a phishing attempt?
questions.teaching_point: Spotting obvious red flags like generic greetings, mismatched domains (gmail.com), and non-HTTPS links.

headers.subject: URGENT: Your account has been locked!

body.content: We detected unusual activity on your account. To prevent permanent deletion, you must verify your identity immediately.

clues.label: Sender Address
clues.explanation: Amazon would never use a @gmail.com address for official account security alerts.

clues.label: Greeting
clues.explanation: Generic greetings like 'Dear Customer' are common in mass phishing campaigns.

clues.label: Link URL
clues.explanation: The link uses 'http' instead of 'https' and the domain 'amazon-update-center.info' is not an official Amazon domain.

emails.explanation: This email is a textbook example of phishing: it uses a free email provider, a generic greeting, high urgency, and a suspicious non-secure link.

body.content: Great news! Your order #123-456789 has been shipped and is on its way to you.

clues.label: Sender Address
clues.explanation: The email comes from the official @amazon.com domain.

clues.label: Personalization
clues.explanation: The email uses the customer's actual name ('Sarah') rather than a generic greeting.

emails.explanation: This is a legitimate transactional email. It uses the correct domain, personalized greeting, and a secure HTTPS link to the official website.

questions.instruction: One of these DHL shipment alerts is fake. Can you find the subtle clue?
questions.teaching_point: Identifying 'look-alike' domains and professional-looking but fraudulent URLs.

body.content: Your shipment is currently on hold at our sorting center due to an incomplete delivery address.
Please update your shipping details to avoid the package being returned to the sender.

clues.label: Sender Domain
clues.explanation: The domain 'dhl-parcel-tracking.net' is a look-alike. Official DHL emails typically come from 'dhl.com'.

clues.label: URL Destination
clues.explanation: The link points to 'dhl-delivery-status.com', which is not the official DHL corporate domain.

emails.explanation: This is a medium-difficulty phish. It uses HTTPS and a professional tone, but the domain is a look-alike designed to trick users who don't check the exact domain name.

headers.subject: Your DHL Express shipment is arriving today

body.content: Your package with tracking number 10001234567890 is out for delivery and is expected to arrive by 6 PM today.

clues.label: Domain Verification
clues.explanation: The sender and the link both use the official and verified 'dhl.com' domain.

emails.explanation: This is a legitimate notification. The domain is the exact corporate domain of the company, and there are no requests for personal information or urgent payment.

questions.instruction: These corporate emails look identical in style. Inspect the headers and domains carefully.
questions.teaching_point: Detecting high-fidelity phishing through precise domain analysis (subdomains vs. main domains).

headers.subject: Action Required: Annual Tax Document Review

body.content: The annual tax review for the current fiscal year is now open. Please review your documents and sign the electronic acknowledgement by Friday.

clues.label: Domain Analysis
clues.explanation: The company's official domain is 'corp.com'. The sender is using 'corp-payroll.com', which is a separate registered domain, not a subdomain of 'corp.com'.

clues.label: URL Logic
clues.explanation: The destination 'corp-payroll-portal.com' is another external domain designed to look internal.

emails.explanation: This is a highly polished phish. It avoids urgent language to build trust and uses a domain that looks like a corporate extension. Only a strict check of the root domain (corp.com vs corp-payroll.com) reveals the fraud.

headers.subject: Your monthly payslip is now available

body.content: Hello, your payslip for the period of October 2023 has been uploaded to the employee portal.

clues.label: Subdomain Verification
clues.explanation: The link 'payroll.corp.com' is a legitimate subdomain of the primary corporate domain 'corp.com'.

emails.explanation: This is a legitimate internal email. The sender address is exactly on the corporate domain, and the link is a proper subdomain of that same corporate domain.
